## 1. The structural theorem

Let \(E:M_a\to M_b\) be a finite-dimensional quantum channel. On its joint output support, define
\[
\Omega_E=E(I_a),\qquad
T_E(X)=\Omega_E^{-1/2}E(X)\Omega_E^{-1/2}.
\]
The map \(T_E\) is unital and completely positive. Form
\[
\mathcal A_E=C^*(T_E(M_a)),
\qquad
\tau_E(Z)=\frac1a\operatorname{Tr}(\Omega_E Z).
\]

Here \(\tau_E\) is a faithful state; it need not be a trace.

For two channels with the same input, the following are equivalent:

1. Their RLD quadratic profiles agree for every finite untouched reference, every faithful input baseline and every traceless Hermitian tangent.
2. All ordered moments of their normalized output generators agree under their respective faithful states.
3. There is an input-labelled, state-preserving unital \(*\)-isomorphism
   \[
   \theta:\mathcal A_\Phi\longrightarrow\mathcal A_\Psi,
   \qquad
   \theta T_\Phi=T_\Psi,
   \qquad
   \tau_\Psi\theta=\tau_\Phi.
   \]
4. All their complete maximal-perspective profiles agree.

The last conclusion actually extends to continuous functional calculus on the relevant positive spectra. It is stronger than equality for one selected divergence.

### The greatest representative

Let \(\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}\) be the ordinary trace-preserving conditional expectation onto \(\mathcal A_E\), and put
\[
Z_E=\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}(\Omega_E).
\]
Define
\[
\boxed{\Gamma_E(X)=Z_E^{1/2}T_E(X)Z_E^{1/2}.}
\]

This is a physical channel. Indeed,
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\Gamma_E(X)
=\operatorname{Tr}Z_ET_E(X)
=\operatorname{Tr}\Omega_ET_E(X)
=\operatorname{Tr}X.
\]
Its normalized output map is again \(T_E\), and its faithful state agrees with \(\tau_E\) on the generated algebra. Consequently, \(\Gamma_E\) belongs to the same complete-profile class.

There is an explicit deterministic operation taking it back to \(E\):
\[
\boxed{
\mathcal R_E(Y)=
\Omega_E^{1/2}Z_E^{-1/2}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}(Y)
Z_E^{-1/2}\Omega_E^{1/2}.
}
\]
Complete positivity follows from the displayed composition, while
\[
\mathcal R_E^*(I)
=
Z_E^{-1/2}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}(\Omega_E)Z_E^{-1/2}
=I.
\]
Thus \(\mathcal R_E\) is trace preserving and
\[
\mathcal R_E\Gamma_E=E.
\]

The map is the established Petz transpose operation. The role it plays here is to recover the original outputs from the **newly constructed lifted outputs** \(\Gamma_E(X)\). Those generally differ from the ordinary coarse-graine

## 3. The construction stays rational and polynomial

The normalized formulas contain square roots. I removed them from the principal algorithm.

Work instead with the raw product
\[
X\star_EY=X\Omega_E^+Y,
\]
where \(\Omega_E^+\) is the Moore–Penrose inverse. Its identity is \(\Omega_E\). All these matrices are rational-complex when the channel is.

For channels \(\Phi,\Psi\), close the paired generators under this product, retaining a basis of actual words. There are at most
\[
N=(\operatorname{rank}\Omega_\Phi)^2+
  (\operatorname{rank}\Omega_\Psi)^2
\]
basis elements. Complete-profile equality holds exactly when
\[
\operatorname{Tr}B_j=\operatorname{Tr}C_j
\]
for every retained pair.

Accepted words have length at most \(N-1\). Their rational bit lengths, the number of multiplications and the exact rank computations are polynomial in the explicitly supplied Choi matrices.

If equality fails, the algorithm converts a differing word into an actual faithful rational state pair. It evaluates a finite rational grid of path pencils, producing a nonzero exact profile difference with reference dimension at most \(N\). The output includes a positive spectral floor and a computable margin.

### Constructing the greatest channel without irrational factors

For the self-comparison of \(E\), let \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) be the raw algebra basis. Define
\[
G_{ij}=\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(\Omega_E^+B_i^*\Omega_E^+B_j\bigr),
\qquad
v_i(Y)=\operatorname{Tr}
\bigl(\Omega_E^+B_i^*\Omega_E^+Y\bigr),
\]
and
\[
L_E(Y)=\sum_j B_j[G^{-1}v(Y)]_j.
\]

This rational map is the normalized conditional expectation expressed in raw coordinates. It is completely positive and fixes every output of \(E\). Let
\[
K_E=L_E^*(I).
\]
Then \(K_E\) is rational, positive on the joint output support, and
\[
\operatorname{Tr}K_EE(X)=\operatorname{Tr}X.
\]

The remaining operation is an exact rational factorization
\[
C^*C=K_E.
\]
A rectangular rational factor always exists, with polynomial size. Rational positive-semidefinite elimination reduces the problem to expressing a positive rational number \(n/m\) as a sum of rational squares. Write \(nm\) in binary: an even power of two is a square, and an odd power is the sum of two equal squares. Dividing by \(m^2\) completes the construction. Integer factorization is unnecessary.

The resulting channel is
\[
\boxed{\Gamma_C(X)=CE(X)C^*.}
\]
It is CP and trace

## 4. What the physical implementation requires

The formula \(\Gamma_C=\operatorname{Ad}_C\circ E\) is not permission to apply \(C\) deterministically to an existing channel output. Generally \(C^*C\npreceq I\).

The valid device construction uses the complete channel description. If \(K_\alpha\) are Kraus operators for \(E\), the new channel has Kraus operators
\[
\widetilde K_\alpha=CK_\alpha,
\qquad
\sum_\alpha\widetilde K_\alpha^*\widetilde K_\alpha=I_a.
\]
These give an actual Stinespring isometry
\[
V|\psi\rangle
=\sum_\alpha\widetilde K_\alpha|\psi\rangle\otimes|\alpha\rangle,
\]
and the actual complementary channel follows from
\[
\Gamma_C^c(X)_{\alpha\beta}
=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(
\widetilde K_\alpha X\widetilde K_\beta^*
\right).
\]

The compiler emits this data. On the preserved capacity-separating fixture, it produced an explicit rational greatest channel with input dimension \(2\), output dimension \(8\), and an environment of dimension \(16\), together with its complement and a deterministic simulator for the high channel.

### Recovery from an existing device has a paid success probability

For a class member \(\Phi\) and target \(\Psi\), let
\[
L\Phi=\Psi,\qquad K=L^*(I).
\]
Choose a rational \(p>0\) with \(pK\preceq I\); for example,
\[
p=\frac1{\operatorname{Tr}K}.
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal S=pL,\qquad
\mathcal F(Y)=\operatorname{Tr}[(I-pK)Y]|\perp\rangle\langle\perp|
\]
form a physical success/failure instrument.

For every referenced input,
\[
(\mathcal S\otimes\mathrm{id})(\Phi\otimes\mathrm{id})(\rho)
=p(\Psi\otimes\mathrm{id})(\rho).
\]
The success probability is independent of the input. Both branches have explicit Kraus realizations, and their environments are included.

Consequently, an \(n\)-use adaptive target protocol has an exact all-success simulation with probability \(p^n\). For an experiment whose initial state can be prepared afresh, the fixed-block convention costs
\[
\frac{n}{p^n}
\]
expected primitive channel uses per accepted block, plus its classical communication.

An unknown input can be destroyed by failure. It cannot generally be retried. This distinction remains part of the theorem.

\quad\text{for every }F\text{ in the class}.
